page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system includes 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core, and is provisioned with 66 GB of local storage alongside Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor delivers weak single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1246.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 848.0. Multi-core performance is average under stress-ng at 6563.83, but falls into the weak category under Geekbench multi-core testing at 3121.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds measured at 35.34 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 21.67 GB/sec. Cryptographic and decompression tasks show lower-tier performance, as evidenced by a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 20.77 GB/sec.

Despite these constraints, the server demonstrates average performance in small-scale language model tasks, achieving 411.44 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 157.1 tokens/sec for text generation using a 135M model. Given its balanced resource density and older processor architecture, this instance represents a standard general-purpose tier. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, basic database operations, and general-purpose application hosting that require Premium Storage compatibility but do not demand high-performance compute or memory-optimized configurations.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 66 GB of local storage with Premium Storage support. Performance benchmarks indicate generally weak single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, alongside limited memory bandwidth. However, it maintains average performance in small-scale LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation for a 135M model. Lacking a GPU and featuring a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including standard web serving, basic database operations, and development environments that benefit from Premium Storage compatibility without requiring high-performance compute resources.
